| S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE | 2026-05-06 | Fix the rate-lookup endpoint at `api/v1/leases/lookup_rates.php` — query by `equipment_templates.category` instead of `equipment_templates.name`. Bug surfaced as a bonus finding during S-MILEAGE-RATE-ZERO-FIX (commit bc4db87) and immediately spawned as carry-forward. **This is the upstream root cause of the entire zero-rate bug class** — fixing it stops new $0-rate leases from being created at the source by closing the silent fall-through that landed every Priority 1 + Priority 2 lookup on Priority 3 (template defaults). 2 commits + this docs entry. **Pre-work scan (Explore agent + direct grep across api/, app/, lib/, scripts/, tests/, cron/, db_migrations/, database/):** all 18 customer_equipment_rates rows + 18 rate_card_items rows + 11 customer_rate_history rows are category-form (`dry_van`, `chassis`, `reefer`, `flatbed`, `container`, `step_deck`, `lowboy`, `tanker`, `dump`); zero rows in template-name form. demo_seed.php + seed_dataset.php WRITE category-form. UI dropdowns at customers/show.php:980 + rates/create.php:173 + rates/show.php:238 WRITE template-name form via `$t['name']` — but UI write activity has been zero on live data (all rows came from seeds). Reports (api/v1/reports/{revenue,fleet}.php, compliance/index.php) read `equipment_templates.category` directly — never touch the rate tables for type matching. lookup_rates.php is the ONLY rate-matching reader; everything else is form-write or display-read. **Decision: Option A** (change lookup line 82 from `$template['name']` to `$template['category']`). Reasoning: (1) `equipment_templates.category` is an ENUM with finite values; `equipment_templates.name` is mutable VARCHAR(100). (2) Multiple templates can share a category — template 1 "53ft Dry Van" + template 6 "Seed: 53ft Dry Van Wabash" both = `dry_van` — per-category rate semantics are correct, per-template-name would fragment them. (3) Live data is already 100% category-form so zero data migration needed. (4) Option B (migrate data + seeds to template names) would have moved the schema in the wrong direction (away from the ENUM). **Commit 1 — fix ([7a45534](api/v1/leases/lookup_rates.php)):** single-line semantic change (`$equipmentType = $template['category']`) plus 17-line docblock rewrite at lines 79-95 explaining the canonical convention, the historical bug, and the carry-forward UX issue (UI dropdowns still write template names). **Commit 2 — smoke ([7941148](tests/_smoke_lookup_rates.php)):** new end-to-end test covering all 4 priority paths via parent/child fork pattern (borrowed from tests/_smoke_payoff_api.php since the endpoint exits via json_response). T1+T2 customer hits on known cust/tmpl pairs (cust=1+tmpl=1 → $0.18/km dry_van, cust=4+tmpl=5 → $0.13/km chassis); T3 rate_card hit using customer 9 SMOKE-S4 test co (zero cer rows) + tmpl=1; T4 + T5 use two temporary `equipment_templates` with category='other' inserted by the parent (one with non-null defaults for Priority 3, one with NULL defaults for Priority 4); both deleted in finally regardless of outcome (test-pollution discipline — confirmed zero `__SMOKE_LOOKUP_RATES%` rows remain post-run). Plus a CONTROL assertion that the pre-fix query shape (template names) returns 0 rows on live data while the post-fix shape (categories) returns >0 — the smoking gun that the bug existed and was correctly identified. 6/6 pass. **Triple-check verification:** (1) PHP lint clean both files; (2) D131 gate green — parity smoke "PARITY OK" 7.0s + invariants smoke "INVARIANTS OK" (I1+I2+I3 untouched); (3) idempotent re-run of smoke (each run uses fresh template IDs since auto-increment moves forward; cleanup verified). **Bonus carry-forward (NOT addressed in this session):** `S-RATES-UI-CATEGORY-DEDUP` — the 3 UI dropdowns still submit template names from `<option value="<?= $t['name'] ?>">`. Net effect today is invisible (zero UI write activity), but a future operator using the form would silently write a row that lookup ignores. Fix requires UX decision: dedup the dropdown to show categories (one option per category with a friendly label) OR show template names but submit category values (visual ambiguity if 2 templates share a category). Out of scope here because it's a UX call, not a code fix. **NOT touched:** UI dropdowns (deferred to S-RATES-UI-CATEGORY-DEDUP); API validators at api/v1/customer_equipment_rates/upsert.php + api/v1/rate_cards/create.php (currently `clean_string` only, no enum validation — could add ENUM constraint when UI is fixed); seed scripts (already write correct category form); `FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql` (no schema changes — query semantic change only); `.env` / FF_ASSET_VERSION (server-side change, no asset cache implication); rate_card_history (no such table — rate_cards has audit_log only). **Carry-forward:** S-RATES-UI-CATEGORY-DEDUP (3 dropdowns + 2 API validators); separately, S-MILEAGE-RATE-VALIDATION (parallel to S-BILLING-RATE-FIX C2/C3/C4 defensive layers — already queued, runs next after this entry lands). **KEY LEARNINGS:** (1) **Docblock vs reality drift** — the lookup_rates.php docblock confidently asserted "rate_card_items.equipment_type and customer_equipment_rates.equipment_type both store this as a string matching the template name" (line 80-81 pre-fix). The docblock was the source of the bug: someone wrote the lookup matching the docblock's claim, but the actual data (written by separate seed scripts) used a different convention. The docblock had been wrong since seed and survived multiple passes through review. Treat docblocks as claims to verify against the data, not as authoritative spec — and when docblocks are corrected, write WHY the prior claim was wrong so the next reader knows the trap. (2) **Pre-work agent scope** — the Explore agent inventory found 14+ readers/writers in <600 words; the inline DB queries cross-checked the agent's assertions against actual data values. Combining the two (agent for breadth + DB for ground truth) is a reliable pattern when the question is "what value-space does this column actually hold". The agent on its own may misread variable names (the agent's "Decision" recommendation in this case proposed Option B based on the assumption that UI dropdowns submit template names — true, but it missed that the UI has zero live-write activity, which made Option A correct without UI changes). (3) **Smoke-test temp data discipline** — to test the Priority 3 + Priority 4 paths required temporary equipment_templates with category='other' (the only category with no rate_card_items entries). The smoke inserts both upfront, runs all 5 tests, deletes them in a finally block. Each run uses fresh auto-increment IDs (visible in the PASS lines as `tmpl_id=22, 23` then `24, 25` etc.) — that's the expected cost of test isolation; the cleanup is verified by `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM equipment_templates WHERE name LIKE '__SMOKE_LOOKUP_RATES%'` returning 0 post-run. |

(c) **Print emulation** via preview_eval — injected both @media print blocks as @media all in a `<style>` element, walked DOM for visible position:fixed elements with dark backgrounds + non-zero rect + ancestor-visibility; pre-fix scan reproduced the overlay (search-overlay rgba(0,0,0,0.5) + modal-backdrop rgba(0,0,0,0.7)), post-fix scan reports zero overlays across all 3 reference invoices. (d) **Operator visual T1 PASS** — confirmed after C3-T1-FIX deployed and `.env` FF_ASSET_VERSION bumped 1.0.25 → 1.0.26 (uncommitted, gitignored). **NOT touched**: api/v1/invoices/show.php (server-side load was sufficient; AJAX endpoint unaffected); FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql (no schema change); FLEETFORGE_SPEC_FINAL.md / FLEETFORGE_ACCOUNTING_SPEC.md (no spec-text change — display work is in DECISIONS table + REFERENCE.md only if needed); FLEETFORGE_DESIGN_DETAILS.md (no new design tokens — extends existing patterns); Mileage Review card + Odometer & Distance card + Rate Explanation card (D-E exclusion held — these are S-MILEAGE-2B territory). **Carry-forward**: (a) S-MILEAGE-2A inherits the line-item dispatch contract + dual S-MILEAGE-2B extension markers — no code reshape needed when adding `mileage_drawdown_credit` / `mileage_usage` line types, just config + match-case + template fragment; (b) S-REVIEW-MILEAGE-TAX-FIX dormant tax-math bug (queued earlier in S-MILEAGE-ALLOWANCE-ZERO-FIX) remains exercisable post-2A when Model B Lite flows through review approval; (c) production cache invalidation: production deploy needs FF_ASSET_VERSION 1.0.25 → 1.0.26 bump in production .env to invalidate cached app.css with old print hide list. **KEY LEARNINGS**: K-13 locked — global include CSS as universal print concern (see KEY LEARNINGS table). Secondary learnings inline: (1) **Pre-flight render emulation as auth-free visual proof** — PHP CLI render with faked $_SESSION + regex extraction of marker patterns produces lossless markup verification without needing real auth; combined with `preview_eval` CSS injection (@media print → @media all) gives screenshot-quality visual proof of print rendering, all under operator-controlled local execution. Cheaper than the K-1-class "share dev test user credentials" pattern when the verification is structural rather than interactive. (2) **Synthetic data via BEGIN/ROLLBACK as a test-pollution-free seam** — applies for any T1 that needs to verify a rendering against a data shape that doesn't yet exist in production data (`credit_note_applications` was empty at lock time). Pattern: insert in a transaction, render, validate, ROLLBACK, post-rollback verify no orphan rows. Matches the `tests/_stress_*.php` BEGIN/ROLLBACK pattern from S-MILEAGE-ALLOWANCE-ZERO-FIX C1. (3) **Operator refinement on tooltip wording surfaces the right audit question** — my initial proposal "Applied to: line #1, #2, #4" forced the accountant to mentally cross-reference line numbers. Operator refinement "Applied to N taxable lines totaling $X" answers the actual reconciliation question ("does the tax base reconcile to the taxable subtotal?") in one read. Surfacing tooltip wording for sign-off rather than shipping the first draft prevented a UX-debt accumulation. |

Here GPS differs from insurance/warranty in two specific places (default opt_in true vs false, per-day billing vs flat-per-period); everything else matches verbatim. The pre-work surfacing of all 7 reference files BEFORE writing code prevented divergence by accident. Pattern: when adding a parallel feature, list every layer the existing feature touches, copy the exact form, then deliberately mark the divergences. Anything unmarked stays identical. (2) **K-9 — COMMENT clauses in migration DDL.** First migration apply produced a parity FAIL because the ADD COLUMN DDL strings omitted the COMMENT clause that master schema needs for documentation parity. The `ff_add_column_if_missing` helper short-circuits if the column already exists, so a re-run won't add the COMMENT after-the-fact. Fix pattern: include the COMMENT clause in the initial DDL string AND issue a separate idempotent `ALTER TABLE … MODIFY COLUMN … COMMENT` for the case where the column was already added in a prior dev iteration (or to fix up a partial application). When updating the file post-apply also update schema_migrations.checksum to match. The migration file pattern from S-MILEAGE-1 (precharge_*) used double-quoted DDL with single-quoted COMMENT — copy verbatim. (3) **K-10 — Operator confirmation on backfill default.** D-G presented two options: (i) default 1.00 on schema → all existing leases auto-bill $1/day; (ii) explicit UPDATE to 0.00 → existing leases preserved at no-billing. The original ticket's plan was option (ii). The user's "$1/day default" directive was ambiguous on backfill semantics. Surfaced the tradeoff explicitly with a recommendation (default ii); operator picked (i). Pattern: when a directive could plausibly mean either of two operationally-distinct outcomes (especially one that touches existing customer billing), surface both with stakes, recommend the safer default, let operator pick. The 3-line `Confirm (i) or (ii)?` prompt was the right cost for the decision. |

The earlier classification was technically defensible from the code's perspective but missed the operator's mental model. Pattern: when classifying an ambiguous shape, surface the proposed disposition before writing fix code — operator may have a different model than the code's. Reconciliation: trust the latest committed state when it's correct; delete duplicates locally; document the reconciliation explicitly in the SESSION LOG. The D131 gate ran clean post-reconciliation, validating the merged state. Pattern: when discovering parallel agent work, verify smoke gates pass on the combined state before continuing — don't blindly revert or rewrite. (4) **K-7 — Engine fix vs. defensive layer trade-off.** D133 added defensive validation to reject (allowance>0 + rate=0) at lease-create time. D135 takes the opposite approach for the (allowance=0 + rate>0) shape: instead of rejecting at create-time, FIX the engine to process the shape correctly. The choice between "reject upstream" vs "process correctly" hinges on whether the shape represents real business intent. When it does, reject is wrong; when it doesn't, reject is correct. This session: rate>0 + allowance=0 IS real intent ("bill every km"), so engine fix is correct; rate=0 + allowance>0 is NOT real intent ("operator forgot to set rate"), so reject is correct. |

Lease 52 duplicate-INV-89/90 anomaly noted but not auto-resolved — operator's call (likely covered by S-LEASE-21-CLEANUP-style cleanup or routine void). **KEY LEARNINGS:** (1) **K-2 — Diagnostic-first protocol for ambiguous bug-vs-correct-behavior.** When an operator flags "X looks wrong" without a clear classification, structure the pre-work to disambiguate three branches before writing code: (a) REAL BUG — math says one thing, code does another → fix; (b) CORRECT BEHAVIOR misunderstood as bug → document + improve visualization; (c) VALIDATION GAP — code is internally consistent but a data shape it doesn't anticipate falls through silently → upstream guard. The classification is a 15-minute investigation that determines whether you're shipping a bug fix, a docs commit, or a queued follow-up. Skipping the diagnostic and jumping to "fix the symptom" risks fixing the wrong layer (e.g. patching InvoiceGenerator when the real fix is at lease create-time). Mirrors the diagnostic protocol used in S-MILEAGE-MODEL-AUDIT and S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE. (2) **K-3 — Defensive auto-fill guards surface anomalies cleanly.** The C2 over-invoiced anomaly guard (`period_start > ceiling`) was added to handle a hypothetical edge case during stress testing — but it actually surfaces a real anomaly in production data (lease 52's duplicate INV-89/90). The operator sees a clear warning at the form ("prior invoice ended past lease ceiling — manual review needed") instead of producing an invalid period_start > period_end. Pattern: when auto-fill logic encounters impossible combinations of inputs, prefer to skip + warn over silently producing nonsense, even if the input combination "shouldn't happen." The guard becomes both a UX improvement and a debugging aid. |

Optional future polish: (a) harden the alternate mileage-line-item insert paths in review_mileage.php + close.php with the same throw — low priority because those are operator-mediated paths; (b) S-LEASE-21-CLEANUP per KNOWN ISSUES A4 — lease 21 has multiple data anomalies (A2 INV-84 period outside lease span; A4 same-day create→close suggests seed/test data); voids alone close I5 but leave the underlying lease state for later cleanup → RESOLVED 2026-05-13 via S-LEASE-21-CLEANUP (KI #107, disposition C — seed/test data); (c) S-RATES-UI-CATEGORY-DEDUP from S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE carry-forward (3 dropdowns + 2 API validators); (d) consider extending D130 wording to cover scope CONTRACTION explicitly per K-NEXT KEY LEARNING below. **KEY LEARNINGS:** (1) **K-NEXT — Silent scope contraction is a recurring discipline gap.** S-MILEAGE-RATE-ZERO-FIX C1 contracted scope twice (dropped smoke gate work AND dropped INV-27/INV-84 voids) without explicit operator re-authorization or SESSION LOG diff at the moment of contraction. Both pieces surfaced later as "discoveries" in S-MILEAGE-RATE-VALIDATION pre-work + I5 trip. Per D130 spirit (currently scoped to expansion, broaden to contraction): any mid-session scope change requires explicit operator re-authorization + SESSION LOG note at the moment it happens, not retrospective recovery in a future session. The retrospective recovery worked here because both pieces were caught quickly (same day) by the next session's pre-work + smoke gate, but the discipline gap means neither catch was guaranteed — different gating could have shipped silent under-billing to a customer. Consider extending D130 wording to cover contraction explicitly: "any mid-session scope change (expansion OR contraction) requires explicit operator re-authorization + SESSION LOG note at the moment it happens". This applies to ALL sessions going forward. (2) **HARD-vs-SOFT split for two-mode failure** — D-B (throw) and D-C (warning) reflect two distinct failure modes for the same observable symptom (mileage block produces no charge). Allowance configured + rate=0 = data hole that demands fail-loud (the D132-class bug pattern). No allowance configured + rate=0 + distance recorded = possible misconfiguration that's also a legitimate "no per-km billing" state (operator chose not to bill mileage on this lease). Mixing the two into a single throw would over-trigger on the legitimate case; the soft signal (Sentry warning + audit_log) is the right severity for the ambiguous state. The pattern: when refusing-to-execute would block legitimate operator intent, downgrade to warn-and-continue with a clear diagnostic the operator can investigate. (3) **Reuse existing exception via context array** — `BillingRateException`'s constructor was billing-tier-specific (method/daily/weekly/monthly) but its `$context` field is the extension point. Mileage-specific fields (estimated_mileage_km, mileage_rate_km, period_distance_km) fit cleanly without a constructor change. The class stays cohesive (one exception type for "billing rate failed") rather than spawning a sibling MileageBillingException; the `method` discriminator (`'mileage_excess'`) lets log readers grep for the new case without ambiguity. When extending an existing exception class, prefer the context array over constructor changes. (4) **Stage-split a multi-condition gate to attach a throw** — the original gate was a single 4-condition AND; refactoring it into "expected" (3 conditions) + "rate check" (1 condition) made the throw natural. The pattern: when adding a throw to silent-skip code, find the conditions that mean "this code SHOULD run" and the conditions that mean "this code can run safely" — the throw goes between them. The split makes the intent explicit and is a one-line readability win even without the throw. |

| D116 | Wider-window bookend strategy: query Samsara `/fleet/vehicles/stats/history` over period ±24h, prefer the last reading at-or-before period start (bookendLow) and first reading at-or-after period end (bookendHigh); fall back to earliest/latest in wider window if no bracketing reading exists; only fail with `reason='no_readings_in_period'` when wider window is also empty. 90-day total range cap returns `reason='period_too_long'` (S-MILEAGE-1B / D-A) | Mainland's fleet is mostly trailers that report at least daily but not always exactly on period boundaries. Locked by Avi pre-execution. The wider-window primary path matches the operational reality of trailers that ping once a day at variable times. | D136 | Multi-agent discipline (locked 2026-05-07 via S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL; extended 2026-05-11 via S-D136-COMMIT-DISCIPLINE): only one write-mode Code Desktop session at a time should be active on `/Users/avi/Documents/fleetforge`. **Default mode:** single-agent serialization on main. Every session start runs a pre-flight read of CURRENT_SESSIONS.md and halts for operator direction if any other session is marked IN-FLIGHT with overlapping file domains. **Read-only exemption:** audits, surveys, decision-surfacing, and any session that does not commit to main are exempt from serialization. They register as `IN-FLIGHT-RO` and may run concurrently with a write-mode session. Multiple IN-FLIGHT-RO sessions may also run concurrently. **Branch isolation fallback:** when the operator explicitly opts into parallel write work, agents use `session/<S-LABEL>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>` branches with the same D131 smoke gate per branch. Merge to main is operator-approved and includes a post-merge smoke run. Both branch SESSION LOG entries document the parallel split. **Author identity caveat:** git's author field is uniform across all Code Desktop agents. Reconstructing parallelism after the fact requires the SESSION LOG narrative + commit timestamps. **Registration commit requirement (locked 2026-05-11 via S-D136-COMMIT-DISCIPLINE):** IN-FLIGHT registration must be COMMITTED to main before any subsequent operation (file edit, DB write, branch creation). Working-tree-only registration does not count as registered. Pre-flight check Step 1.5 (CURRENT_SESSIONS.md `pre-flight check` section) verifies the registration is committed-clean before subsequent edits. **Enforcement:** relies on agent discipline reading CURRENT_SESSIONS.md, same model as D131 (smoke gates) and D127 (parity). No automated locking, no git hooks (MVP — defer until soft lock proves insufficient). The branch isolation fallback addresses collision avoidance, not state-divergence avoidance — without the commit step, a session that registers IN-FLIGHT in working tree and crashes leaves the registration invisible to a fresh agent reading the file, and a downstream session can create a branch from working-tree carryover state. Backfilled here in S-DOCS-CLUSTER-2026-05-11 (D-D); the decision had already been locked in REFERENCE.md §0 LOCKED DECISIONS via S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL (commit f195bee) but was not yet in this DECISIONS table — gap surfaced by S-D136-COMMIT-DISCIPLINE pre-work scan. | S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL (commit f195bee) locks the base discipline. | D188 | users.mfa_verified_until semantics (locked 2026-05-14 via S-AUTH-FIX D-A): NULL = MFA has never been blessed for this user via a remember-me cycle — re-prompt MFA on session restoration. NOT NULL = the datetime at which the MFA blessing expires. If NOW() < mfa_verified_until, auth_check_remember_me() skips the MFA challenge and restores the full session. If expired, the remember-me cycle still restores the session at password level (auth_login runs) but sets `$_SESSION['ff_mfa_pending']` so the next request is gated on MFA re-verification. Net effect: "Keep me signed in for 30 days" covers BOTH factors for 30 days from MFA completion, then transitions to a clean MFA re-prompt (not a full logout). ## KEY LEARNINGS — searchable index

Standalone index of cross-session lessons learned. SESSION LOG entries above retain their per-session learnings inline (chronological narrative); this section is the searchable subject-by-subject index. Add a new K-* entry when a learning surfaces that's likely to apply across sessions, not just the one that surfaced it.

| # | Date | Subject | Learning |
|---|------|---------|----------|
| K-1 | 2026-05-07 | **Namespace mismatch bug pattern** (S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE) | When a docblock asserts a column contract that doesn't match actual data convention, the upstream lookup chain silently fails (returns NULL or zero rows; downstream consumers see "no match" as a fall-through, not as an error). Fix protocol: (1) scan ALL writers + readers to identify the dominant convention — don't trust the docblock. (2) Align the outlier (usually the queries, not the data — cheaper, no migration). (3) Update the docblock to match reality, with WHY the prior claim was wrong so the next reader knows the trap. (4) Add test coverage proving the lookup yields expected results for production cases, including a CONTROL assertion that the pre-fix query shape returns 0 rows on live data — without this control, a future test reader cannot tell whether the chain "always worked" or was silently broken before the fix. (5) Lock the canonical contract as a D-* decision in PROGRESS.md DECISIONS table AND cite it in REFERENCE.md §0 LOCKED DECISIONS for quick-lookup discoverability. Pattern surfaced in S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE: `lookup_rates.php` was the outlier against the dominant category convention; data was already 100% category-form so zero migration needed; D134 locked the contract going forward. |
| K-11 | 2026-05-07 | **Lock multi-agent discipline before frequency, not after** (S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL) | K-6 (S-MILEAGE-ALLOWANCE-ZERO-FIX same-session overlap, 2026-05-07) was one data point in 177 commits — caught and reconciled cleanly because the parallel edits were additive (two non-overlapping I6 stress tests, additive REFERENCE.md sections, no migration conflicts). The failure modes of (c) accept-and-reconcile escalate non-linearly with concurrency: two agents both ALTER TABLE the same column would corrupt the schema before D131 parity smoke runs. The asymmetry between cost-of-discipline (low: one status field + a pre-flight read) and cost-of-the-second-incident (high: schema corruption, manual DB recovery) means the discipline should be locked at the first incident, not the tenth. Pattern: when a new incident class first appears, run the failure-mode analysis immediately and surface the discipline question — don't wait for recurrence to validate "this is a pattern." S-ACCT-AUDIT (b74b947, same day, different parallel session, SESSION LOG row backfilled in this same commit) confirms the first incident wasn't isolated — concurrency is happening, just not always with conflicts yet. |
| K-13 | 2026-05-11 | **Global include CSS as universal print concern, not page-scoped** (S-INVOICE-DISPLAY-COMPREHENSIVE C3-T1-FIX) | When a CSS class is rendered globally — via `includes/header.php`, `includes/footer.php`, `includes/partials/*` — its print-time behavior is a universal concern across every admin page that uses the standard layout. Hide rules belong in the GLOBAL `@media print` block in `public/assets/css/app.css`, NOT in per-page page-scoped `<style>` blocks. The page-scoped print block is for elements unique to that page (e.g., the invoice's letterhead, financial summary card, line items table). Surfaced via the `.search-modal` (a.k.a. `#ff-search-modal`) incident in S-INVOICE-DISPLAY-COMPREHENSIVE T1: search modal is rendered globally via `includes/footer.php` on every admin page; uses Alpine `x-show="open"` for visibility (default `open: false`). When the modal is open at print time — or Alpine fails to apply hide before the print engine captures the DOM — its `.search-overlay` child paints `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` over the entire viewport, producing a dark semi-transparent overlay. The page-scoped `@media print` in `show.php` hid `.modal-overlay` (covering void/delete/confirm/email modals) but NOT `.search-modal` — a page-scoped fix would have hidden the overlay on /invoices/show only, leaving every OTHER admin page's print still broken. The right fix is one-line in app.css's `@media print` hide list adding `.search-modal, .search-overlay, .modal-overlay, .modal-backdrop, .sidebar-overlay`. Pattern: when adding `@media print` hide rules, ask "is this class rendered by an include?" If yes → app.css `@media print`. If no → page-scoped `<style>`. Diagnostic: grep `class="<X>"` across `includes/` to determine universality before scoping the fix. The cost-of-discipline (one extra grep at fix-time) versus cost-of-no-discipline (universal bug fixed per-page, only the page that surfaced the bug benefits, every other admin print still ships the regression). |
| K-12 | 2026-05-07 | **Documentation divergence is its own bug class** (S-DOC-STATUS-RECONCILE-CLOSE) | S-QUEUE-STATUS-RECONCILE diagnostic surfaced 4 cases where actual ship state (git log + commits) diverged from declared state (CURRENT_SESSIONS.md status / PROGRESS.md SESSION LOG). Cause: post-ship doc updates were skipped or partial during fast session cycling. Cost-of-divergence: operator confusion ("did this ship?"), planning errors ("let me draft this — wait it's already done"), audit trail gaps. Cost-of-prevention: 30 seconds at session-end to update both files. Pattern: every shipping session must close-loop on BOTH CURRENT_SESSIONS.md (mark SHIPPED) AND PROGRESS.md SESSION LOG (write the row) — neither alone is sufficient. The S-QUEUE-STATUS-RECONCILE diagnostic should run periodically (e.g. end of each work day or every N sessions) to catch divergence before it accumulates. D136 plus K-12 together: agents register at session start (CURRENT_SESSIONS.md IN-FLIGHT) AND close-loop at session end (CURRENT_SESSIONS.md SHIPPED + PROGRESS.md SESSION LOG row). Two-sided protocol. |
| K-14 | 2026-05-12 | **Category separation in tracking files — pre-deploy obligations need their own canonical file** (S-PREDEPLOY-CHECKLIST-CREATE) | K-12 ("documentation divergence is its own bug class") established that tracking-file state must match reality. K-14 extends K-12 with a category-separation rule: tracking files have shapes, and filing an item in the wrong-shaped file is itself documentation divergence. Three categories with three canonical files: **(a) bug-shaped** — a defect in shipped code — files to `FLEETFORGE_PROGRESS.md` → KNOWN ISSUES (`#NNN`); **(b) session-shaped** — work that will be a future session — files to `FLEETFORGE_CURRENT_SESSIONS.md` queue; **(c) pre-deploy-shaped** — a `.env` key needing a real prod value, an AWS resource to provision, a DNS record, a smoke/rollback procedure, a monitoring dashboard, a data-state precondition — files to `FLEETFORGE_PREDEPLOY_CHECKLIST.md` in the appropriate category (A asset cache / B prod .env keys / C DNS / D AWS infra / E data migrations / F accounting state / G smoke / H rollback / I monitoring / J references). **Why this surfaced as a discipline gap:** before S-PREDEPLOY-CHECKLIST-CREATE there was no canonical pre-deploy file, so pre-deploy obligations accumulated under the wrong categories — `FF_ASSET_VERSION` bumps got noted in SESSION LOG narrative but had no actionable home, AR drift reconciliation was filed as a fix-script with no deploy-time pointer, AWS resource provisioning was scattered across SPEC_FINAL.md + REFERENCE.md + runbooks. Operator pre-work for the cutover would have to walk multiple files cold to find every obligation. **The discipline is two-sided:** (i) when filing a new obligation, route it to the correct file category before writing; (ii) when reading any tracking file, the file's stated category defines what belongs there — a pre-deploy obligation in KNOWN ISSUES is misfiled even if the entry is accurate. Both sides preserved K-12's "divergence is a bug class" framing — the shape of the entry must match the shape of the file. **Pattern for future tracking-file introductions:** when a new category of work-state surfaces that doesn't cleanly belong in any existing tracking file (and the existing files would have to bend their shape to absorb it), the right move is to introduce a new tracking file with its own discipline rule + inventory of pre-existing scattered items, not to overload an existing file. `FLEETFORGE_PREDEPLOY_CHECKLIST.md` is the first such addition since CURRENT_SESSIONS.md was created in S-CURRENT-SESSIONS-FILE. Cross-references locked: REFERENCE.md §0 LOCKED DECISIONS K-14 row + §1 SEVEN FILES "Deployment-time companion" note; CURRENT_SESSIONS.md Pre-flight check section + Documentation cleanup queue SHIPPED entry; AWS Lightsail cutover entry; this PROGRESS.md SESSION LOG row + KEY LEARNINGS row. |
| K-15 | 2026-05-12 | **Data-path coverage discipline for code-class bug remediation** (S-REVIEW-MILEAGE-TAX-FIX) | When a code-class bug is found and remediated for known affected rows, the remediation scope must include ALL rows produced by the buggy code path between bug introduction and bug fix. S-MILEAGE-ALLOWANCE-ZERO-FIX C5 remediated INV-91 via the same shape this session uses for INV-92, but didn't run the equivalent of pre-work scan #7 (full SELECT for ALL `mileage_adjustment` line items) to find OTHER rows produced by the same path. INV-92 had been created at 2026-05-06 22:11:16 via review_mileage.php approve flow — same code, same bug — and got missed. Going forward: when a code-path bug is found AND that path has produced any production data, the remediation pre-work scan must enumerate ALL rows from that path within the bug's lifetime window, not just the inciting row. Same discipline as D129 (re-run grep with NO scope filter before destructive ops) but for data-path coverage. Practical shape: identify the schema artifact the buggy code writes (here: `invoice_line_items.item_type='mileage_adjustment'`) + the time window (here: bug introduction in pre-history through fix commit), then `SELECT *` with no filters except the artifact + the lifetime window, surface all rows for operator decision. Cost: one query. Cost-of-skip: one row of $90.08 under-billing slipped past one full session. The asymmetry favors the discipline. |
| K-16 | 2026-05-12 | **Mid-arc chat handoff discipline** (S-MILEAGE-2A-SPEC-WRITE) | When operator closes a long claude.ai web chat and starts a new one mid-arc, the closing chat's final session must write the next session's full spec into the canonical files (CURRENT_SESSIONS.md + PROGRESS.md if multi-session arc). The new chat reads canonical files via filesystem access; conversation context does not transfer. **Origin:** S-MILEAGE-2A-SPEC-WRITE 2026-05-12, written before closing the long claude.ai web chat that scoped the Model B refactor across multiple sessions. The spec-write session's pre-work scan must verify file:line references against current code state — the closing chat's working memory drifts from reality across long sessions, and writing stale references into the canonical handoff defeats the discipline's purpose. K-12 (documentation divergence as bug class) applies in full: the new chat will trust the canonical files, so the canonical files must be accurate at handoff time. Pattern: the session writing the handoff spec runs a pre-work scan against the actual files-of-record, surfaces any discrepancies between the operator's narrative and current code state, applies corrections under explicit operator authorization (path B in the spec-write decision tree), and notes the corrections transparently in the SESSION LOG row for audit trail. The new chat begins from accurate canonical state, not stale narrative. |
| K-17 | 2026-05-12 | **Branch divergence reconciliation discipline — merge commit, not rebase, when journal files are in scope** (S-FORK-CLOSE-RESOLVE) | When a worktree branch (D136 isolation) and main both accumulate commits independently AND both sides touch live-state-tracking files (`FLEETFORGE_CURRENT_SESSIONS.md`, `FLEETFORGE_PROGRESS.md` SESSION LOG / Recent ship history / KEY LEARNINGS, or any file functioning as a journal of mutable state), **rebase is the wrong tool** — replay-of-historical-snapshots will force conflicts at every commit that touched the journal because each commit captured the journal at a different moment-in-time. **Use merge commit instead**: git's three-way merge handles journal-style files cleanly — single 3-way merge produces editorial-merge decisions (which entries to keep, which order), not impossible reconciliations. Non-linear history is honest representation of genuinely parallel work, not noise. **Pre-merge:** tag the worktree branch as safety net (`pre-rebase-<S-LABEL>-backup` style, push to origin for 30 days), inventory SHA cross-references in canonical docs (none are load-bearing as click-through links — historical narrative refs are time-locked per S-FORK-CLOSE-RESOLVE convention, do not update). **Post-merge:** manual chronological reconciliation of the journal sections (Recent ship history descending UTC within date; SESSION LOG ascending UTC; KEY LEARNINGS table by K-number convention not strict chronology); surface each conflict hunk verbatim BEFORE applying resolutions; operator confirms each. **Origin:** S-FORK-CLOSE-RESOLVE 2026-05-12, when rebase aborted at commit 2/11 due to journal-file conflicts on `claude/kind-sanderson-4ed75d` worktree branch (S-DOCS-CLUSTER + S-INVOICE-DISPLAY-COMPREHENSIVE + S-PREDEPLOY-CHECKLIST-CREATE arcs accumulating in parallel with S-REVIEW-MILEAGE-TAX-FIX on main). Switched to Option B merge commit (ab122eb) and resolved cleanly with 4 conflict hunks across 2 files. **Rebase remains the right tool** for code-only divergence (no journal files in the diverged commits); **merge commit is the right tool** when journal files are in scope. Pre-rebase / pre-merge backup tag is free safety (cost-of-discipline: 10s; cost-of-no-discipline: manual `git reflog` archaeology when something goes sideways). Diagnostic at decision time: `git diff <base>...<branch> -- '<journal-files>'` — if non-empty, prefer merge commit; if empty, rebase is safe. |
| K-18 | 2026-05-12 | **Stress test pre-population can hide bugs in fallback paths** (S-MILEAGE-2B C3.5) | When introducing a fallback gate (e.g., "if caller didn't pre-populate X, fetch X from upstream service"), the happy-path stress test that pre-populates X correctly bypasses the fallback codepath entirely — exercising only the "caller supplied X" branch. The fallback branch can ship broken (e.g., my C3 InvoiceGenerator change accessed `$lease['samsara_vehicle_id']` but the column lives on `equipment_units`, not `leases` — silent null → fallback never fired) and the stress will pass. **Pattern:** when introducing a fallback gate, also write a stress case that explicitly exercises the fallback path (no pre-population + upstream condition that triggers the fetch + assertion that the fetch ran). The 5 cases in `tests/_stress_drawdown_emit.php` all pre-populated `odometer_at_period_*_km` AND created leases without `samsara_vehicle_id` (the lease table doesn't even have the column — it's on `equipment_units`). Either of those guards short-circuits the Samsara fallback, so the broken JOIN bug never surfaced through the stress. Surfaced during pre-C4 INV-87 lookup that selected `l.samsara_vehicle_id` and crashed with "Unknown column" — that's when the bug was caught. Fix landed in C3.5 (commit 64b37cb) with a `LEFT JOIN equipment_units` extension to the lease SELECT. **K-15 adjacency:** K-15 is data-path coverage discipline ("when a code-class bug is found, remediate ALL rows produced by that path"). K-18 is the test-design parallel ("when adding a fallback gate, write a test that proves the fallback works"). Both rest on the discipline "the test that PASSES says nothing about the paths it didn't exercise." Cost of K-18: one additional stress case per fallback introduction. Cost of no K-18: silent production failure in 100% of fallback-eligible invocations. |
| K-19 | 2026-05-12 | **Persistent dev test user — credentials at `/.claude/dev_credentials.json`, NOT recreated each session** (S-MILEAGE-2B-T1-FOLLOWUP, retroactive lock against the K-1 "create + delete each session" pattern that S-MILEAGE-2B-T1 inherited) | K-1 established that Claude Code never reads / requests operator credentials and instead works against a dev-only test user with a disposable password. K-1 originally framed the user as created + deleted within each session ("single-session disposable"). S-MILEAGE-2B-T1 ran that pattern: created user id=22 + Manager role + 16-char password + soft-deleted at tear-down. **Refinement (K-19):** every future browser-automation / preview session that needs an authenticated session will face the same setup tax (create user → bcrypt password → restore unit + lease + fixture state → log in → walk → tear down → soft-delete). Unless the session's scope explicitly demands a fresh user identity (rare — most sessions just need "some authenticated non-super-admin to drive the UI"), persist the user across sessions and only rotate the password when (a) leaked, (b) operator manually flips role/permissions, or (c) annual hygiene. **Implementation:** credentials live at `/.claude/dev_credentials.json` (gitignored under `.gitignore:75` `.claude/`); file is `chmod 600` (rw owner only). JSON shape: `email`, `password` (plaintext — never committed), `role` description, `user_id`, `created_at`, `persisted_at`, `password_rotated_at`, `password_rotation_history` (array — each rotation logged inline), `bcrypt_cost`, `created_by_session`, `persisted_by_session`, `purpose`, `rotation_policy`, `k_compliance`. **Discipline two-sided:** (i) future sessions check for `/.claude/dev_credentials.json` first; if present + login still works, reuse instead of creating fresh. (ii) when rotating, regenerate password via Option (a) (un-soft-delete + reset password + update file) rather than creating a new user_id (preserves audit trail continuity across sessions). **K-1 alignment preserved:** operator credentials still never read by Claude Code; the dev test user is still disposable in principle (operator can delete the row at any time and the next session will re-create); the only refinement is "single-session and delete" → "reuse with optional rotation". **Soft-delete-on-tear-down is the unnecessary cycle K-19 corrects** — it forced S-MILEAGE-2B-T1-FOLLOWUP to un-soft-delete user 22 + rotate password to persist what should have stayed live in the first place. Future T1-style walks: keep the user live + restore unit/lease/fixture state but not the user. |
| K-20 | 2026-05-13 | **Schema column retirement requires repo-wide grep across ALL PHP files, including endpoints outside the primary retirement scope** (S-MILEAGE-3 C5; surfaced by S-MILEAGE-3-FIX-0) | When a DROP COLUMN migration retires a schema column, the pre-DROP grep must enumerate every consumer of the column name across the full codebase — not just the primary retirement scope. **Origin:** S-MILEAGE-2B C4 (commit 840c71f) DROPped 7 Model C columns from invoices including `excess_distance_km`. The C4 session's grep covered the primary retirement scope (close.php + InvoiceGenerator.php + show.php Mileage Review card) but `api/v1/leases/show.php` was outside that scope and retained an orphan `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(excess_distance_km), 0) FROM invoices WHERE lease_id = ?` block. Post-C4 the endpoint's first hit would have failed silently with a MySQL "Unknown column" error (the SELECT was wrapped in db_row which silently catches PDO exceptions and returns null in some legacy paths). **The orphan survived 1 day** until S-MILEAGE-3 C5's broader retirement pass caught it (the priorExcessKm retirement scope happened to overlap with the lease show endpoint via the closeReconciliation Alpine getter's `lease.prior_excess_km` consumption). **Pattern:** after any DROP COLUMN migration, run `grep -rn '<column_name>' api/ lib/ app/ scripts/ tests/` across the full codebase before declaring the retirement complete. Extends D129 (repo-wide grep before helper deletion) to schema column retirement. **Smoke parity gate doesn't catch this class** — the parity smoke checks master ↔ live DB shape consistency (which the DROP itself resolves), not consumer code that still references the dropped name. **K-15 extension secondary learning:** K-15 is data-path WRITE coverage discipline (remediation must cover ALL rows produced by buggy path); K-20 is READ-coverage discipline (retirement must cover ALL queries reading the dropped column too). Both rest on "the test that PASSES says nothing about the paths it didn't exercise." |
| K-21 | 2026-05-13 | **At lease close, any block that reads lease state must fire AFTER all invoice generation completes — and RE-READ from DB, not use cached value** (S-MILEAGE-3-FIX-0; surfaced by S-MILEAGE-3 T1 Step 5) | `InvoiceGenerator::createFromLease()` mutates lease state (precharge_balance drawdown) as a side effect of generating an invoice. Any downstream block in the close transaction that depends on post-generation lease state MUST run AFTER the createFromLease call AND re-read the state from DB via `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` — not use the cached `$lease` array value from the close transaction's opening SELECT. **Origin:** S-MILEAGE-3 C3 placed the refund dispatch block AFTER the lease-close audit_log row but BEFORE the ADV-BILL-1 advance handling + legacy partial-end final-invoice generation. The refund block read `$lease['precharge_balance'] = $77.78` (cached pre-drawdown value) and stamped the cash refund for $77.78. Then the final-invoice generation ran createFromLease, which independently fired the drawdown emit, consumed the same $77.78, and UPDATEd balance to $0. Customer outcome: $77.78 residual applied TWICE (drawdown credit on Invoice 3 + cash refund owed) → $155.56 total benefit from $77.78 residual. **Real financial double-credit, not a display artifact.** Surfaced at T1 Step 5 (KI #106 filed 2026-05-13 commit bda21ec); fixed in S-MILEAGE-3-FIX-0 by (a) moving the refund block to AFTER the final-invoice generation, (b) adding `$leasePostFinal = db_row("SELECT precharge_balance, precharge_refund_method FROM leases WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE", [$id])` re-read immediately before the dispatch logic, (c) keying needsRefund on the re-read $residualBalance rather than the cached $lease value. **Pattern for future close-time work:** if you're adding a block that reads/writes lease state in close.php, ask: "Does any invoice-generation call between transaction-open and this block mutate the column I'm reading?" If yes, re-read FOR UPDATE before consuming. Cost-of-discipline: one SELECT (~1ms). Cost-of-no-discipline: financial double-credit caught only via end-to-end T1 walk. **The smoke I9 invariant didn't catch this** because I9 keys on the persisted state (which was internally consistent: method='cash' + settled_at=NULL was valid), not on the relationship between refund amount and post-drawdown residual. A future I10 candidate: cross-check refund_amount in audit_log against post-final-drawdown precharge_balance — if amount > residual, fail. Locked here as discipline first; smoke candidate deferred to S-MILEAGE-5 scenario coverage. **I10 SHIPPED 2026-05-13 via S-MILEAGE-5** (commit e16d3f6 — both credit branch `credit_notes.amount == leases.precharge_balance` and cash branch `audit_log new_values.amount == leases.precharge_balance` paths, plus the S20 hermetic end-to-end scenario validating the post-drawdown identity holds through the full close-refund flow). |
| K-22 | 2026-05-13 | **Planning-chat prompt drafting must trust on-disk canonical-file state over handoff-prompt narrative** (S-K22-LOCK; sourced from S-CHECKLIST-DRIFT-FIX + S-PROD-2-DOCS-RECONCILE + S-DOCS-REORG-RESIDUAL 2026-05-13) | Before drafting build prompts that depend on factual claims — session status (QUEUED / IN-FLIGHT / SHIPPED), schema state, migration count, or file directional conventions (e.g., `FLEETFORGE_PROGRESS.md` SESSION LOG is ascending chronological oldest-first; `FLEETFORGE_CURRENT_SESSIONS.md` Recent ship history is descending-within-date) — the planning chat MUST verify against the relevant canonical file directly (PROGRESS.md SESSION LOG, CURRENT_SESSIONS.md, FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql, or the target file itself), or include explicit pre-flight verification instructions for Code Desktop. The handoff-prompt narrative is a one-time chat artifact subject to staleness across long planning sessions; canonical-file state is authoritative. **Source incidents (all 2026-05-13):** **(a) S-CHECKLIST-DRIFT-FIX** — prompt's D131 gate spec claimed "migrate 18/0/0" but actual baseline was 17/0/0 (post-S-LEASE-RATE-AMENDMENT option-A reuse meant no migration was added); prompt's SESSION LOG instruction said "insert at top (descending chronological convention)" but actual SESSION LOG is ascending. Code Desktop surfaced both via AskUserQuestion at pre-flight; operator confirmed file-authoritative on both. **(b) S-PROD-2-DOCS-RECONCILE** — prompt arrived as an 8-commit build arc for S-PROD-2 production-readiness instrumentation (Sentry SDK + SES bounce webhook + key rotation runbook + Mailer suppression check), but the work had actually SHIPPED 2026-05-02 per PROGRESS.md SESSION LOG row at line 104 + DECISIONS D75-D78 + production code at `lib/Observability/Sentry.php` + `api/v1/webhooks/ses_notifications.php` + `docs/runbooks/key_rotation.md` + `db_migrations/S-PROD-2_ses_bounce_handler.sql`. The CURRENT_SESSIONS.md QUEUED entry was a phantom introduced earlier the SAME DAY by S-CHECKLIST-DRIFT-FIX C2 based on stale chat-thread info. The prompt's design choices also diverged from shipped reality (separate `email_suppressions` table vs shipped `email_disabled` directly-on-row pattern per D77). Code Desktop surfaced the SHIPPED state pre-flight; operator authorized 3-commit docs-only reconcile instead of the 8-commit build. **(c) S-DOCS-REORG-RESIDUAL** — single-file working-tree residual surfaced at S-CHECKLIST-DRIFT-FIX close, requiring a third docs-only session to git-mv-and-document. **3-session cleanup cost (~45 minutes Code Desktop capacity)** would not have been needed if the originating planning-chat prompts had verified factual claims against on-disk state before issuance. **Pattern:** the planning chat IS the prompt-drafting agent; it must run the same trust-file-over-prompt discipline that Code Desktop runs at pre-flight. Practical workflow for the planning chat: before issuing any prompt that names a session label, a migrate count, an ordering convention, or a schema state — read the relevant canonical file directly via filesystem access (`cat`, `grep`, `head`) and align the prompt's claims to current reality. **Cost-of-discipline:** one file read per factual claim (low). **Cost-of-no-discipline:** Code Desktop catches the drift at pre-flight (good) but the prompt's plan is then partially or wholly invalid, requiring a STOP + AskUserQuestion + scope renegotiation (medium friction); WORSE if the drift is silently rolled forward (high friction — see the S-CHECKLIST-DRIFT-FIX → S-PROD-2-DOCS-RECONCILE pipeline where the first session's drift introduced phantom queue state that the second session had to clean up). **Companion memory entry:** `/Users/avi/.claude/projects/-Users-avi-Documents-fleetforge/memory/feedback_trust_file_over_prompt.md` captures the Code-Desktop-side version of this rule (last extended 2026-05-13 via S-PROD-2-DOCS-RECONCILE close). K-22 captures the planning-chat-side version. Both sides apply the same principle at different scopes: planning chat verifies before issuing; Code Desktop verifies at pre-flight and surfaces discrepancies via AskUserQuestion. |

| NAV-1 | 2026-04-07 | Accounting Nav Fixes (Topnav Dropdown Clipping + Sidebar Restructure) | **3 files modified, 0 new files.** Cross-cutting fix covering both the accounting topnav dropdown bug and the sidebar's accounting section. No new features — pure correctness + consistency. **(1) ROOT CAUSE — topnav dropdowns rendering empty**: `.acc-topnav` in `public/assets/css/app.css` used `overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: visible`. Per CSS spec, setting `overflow-x` to any value other than `visible` silently forces `overflow-y` to a non-`visible` value (the browser computes it to `auto`), which creates a clipping context that hides the absolutely-positioned group dropdown panels. The HTML was correctly rendering all 16 child links (verified via curl), they were just visually clipped. **Fix**: replaced `overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: visible` with `flex-wrap: wrap; overflow: visible`, allowing the nav pill-bar to wrap to a second row on narrow viewports instead of scrolling horizontally, and letting the dropdown panels escape the container cleanly. Added an explanatory comment block about the CSS spec gotcha for future maintainers. **(2) Sidebar accounting section restructured to mirror topnav**: the sidebar previously had 8 individual items (Dashboard, Chart of Accounts, Journal Entries, Accounts Payable, Bank, Tax, Reports, Budgets) — of which 4 (`/accounting/accounts-payable`, `/accounting/tax`, `/accounting/reports`, `/accounting/budgets`) were dead 404s, and the structure didn't match the grouped topnav built in S028-c. Replaced entire accounting section in `config/navigation.php` with a single collapsible "Accounting" parent item (`calculator` icon, `match_prefix => '/accounting'`) containing 8 children: Dashboard, General Ledger, Receivables, Payables, Banking, Fixed Assets, Periods, Settings — exactly matching the 6 functional groups + Periods + Settings in the topnav. Each group child uses a `match_prefix` array listing all sibling URLs so the child stays highlighted across every sub-page in its group (e.g. "General Ledger" child is active on `/accounting/ledger`, `/accounting/chart-of-accounts`, `/accounting/journal-entries`, and `/accounting/reports/trial-balance`). Permissions use the correct module keys: `journal_entries` for Dashboard/GL/Receivables/Settings, `accounts_payable` for Payables, `bank_accounts` for Banking, `fixed_assets` for Fixed Assets, `period_management` for Periods. **(3) `match_prefix` field added to `includes/sidebar.php`**: backward-compatible enhancement — any nav item (parent or child) can now declare an optional `match_prefix` field as either a single string or an array of strings; the active-state detection iterates the prefix list and activates on the first match via `str_starts_with($_currentPath, FF_BASE_PATH . $_mp)`. Falls back to `$_item['url']` when `match_prefix` is not set, so every existing nav item keeps working unchanged. Applied identically to parent active detection, child-active-expansion detection (with `break 2`), and the child render loop. Variable cleanup list updated: added `$_matchPrefixes`, `$_mp`, `$_childPrefixes`, `$_cp`; removed `$_itemFullUrl`, `$_childFullUrl`. **Verification**: (a) Standalone unit test `/tmp/ff_sidebar_test.php` — replicates the sidebar active-state logic against `config/navigation.php` without booting FleetForge, tests all 19 accounting URLs (`/accounting/dashboard`, `/chart-of-accounts`, `/journal-entries`, `/ledger`, `/reports/trial-balance`, `/ar-aging`, `/statements`, `/collections`, `/deposits`, `/bills`, `/ap-aging`, `/vendor-credits`, `/bank-accounts`, `/bank-reconciliation`, `/fixed-assets`, `/depreciation`, `/capex`, `/periods`, `/settings`) and asserts that parent is active + exactly one child is active + child label matches expected group → **19/19 PASS**. (b) HTTP-level test via curl+session against Herd — fetched all 19 pages and confirmed the correct sidebar child carries `is-active` class on every page. (c) Visual verification — Chrome headless screenshots of Fixed Assets, Chart of Accounts, and Statements pages confirming both topnav dropdowns open correctly (no clipping) AND sidebar group highlight synchronizes with the topnav group. **Files modified**: `public/assets/css/app.css` (topnav overflow), `includes/sidebar.php` (match_prefix field), `config/navigation.php` (accounting section restructure). **SC passed**: SC1 php -l all modified files clean ✅; SC2 unit test 19/19 pages pass ✅; SC3 HTTP 19/19 pages render correct sidebar highlight ✅; SC4 topnav dropdown panels visible and not clipped on narrow + wide viewports ✅; SC5 all sidebar child URLs resolve to real pages (no more 404s) ✅. |

'is-invalid' : ''"` input highlighting, `@input`/`@change="errors.X = ''"` self-clearing, and `_paintErrors` called in the `!r.success` branch of every submit handler. **(2) Server API bugs fixed during smoke test** — two endpoints were emitting non-VALID-2 envelopes and got rewritten: **(a) `api/v1/vendors/create.php`** was failing fast with `json_error('MISSING_REQUIRED', …)` and single-field `VALIDATION_ERROR` messages on every guard (name, vendor_type, rating, hourly_rate) — refactored to accumulate every error into a `$fields[]` array, check email format via `clean_email()`, validate hourly_rate ≥ 0, and emit one `json_validation_error($fields)` at the end; duplicate-name uniqueness now also reports through the fields envelope so the client highlights the name field. **(b) `api/v1/yards/create.php`** was using a bespoke `['errors' => [...]]` extra key instead of the standard `fields` + was failing fast on `name` — refactored to accumulate errors (`name`, `capacity` non-negative, `manager_id` existence), emit `json_validation_error($fields)` once, and report name collisions through the same envelope. **(3) Smoke test harness** — `tests/_smoke_valid2.php` (NEW, ~290 lines). Manually writes a real PHP session file to `/var/tmp/sess_<id>` (the path Herd's PHP-FPM uses — **not** CLI PHP's `/var/folders/x6/.../T/`), injects `ff_user` + `ff_last_activity` + a known `csrf_token`, then uses `curl_init()` to POST bad JSON payloads against the live Herd endpoints with `Cookie: ff_session=<id>` + `X-CSRF-Token: <csrf>`. **30 test cases run**, covering every create endpoint in the app: Journal Entry (empty / 1 line / unbalanced), Bank Account (empty / bad currency), Bank Transfer (same source/dest), Bill (empty), Tax Period (bad tax_type / end-before-start), CapEx Request, Vendor Credit, AR Deposit, Customer (empty / bad email / discount > 100 / negative credit limit), Equipment Unit (empty / bad year), Lease, Invoice (empty / period_end before period_start), Payment (empty / negative amount), Vendor, Reservation, Damage Claim, Maintenance WO, Inspection, Mileage Log, Yard. Each case asserts: (a) HTTP 422, (b) `success === false`, (c) `error.code === 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, (d) `error.fields` is a non-empty object containing the expected field keys. **Final run: 30 / 30 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP** — all envelopes shaped correctly, every expected field key present. Test file includes defensive cleanup that `DELETE`s any stray `company_name LIKE 'Smoke Acme%'` customers at the end so regressions can't leak rows into the dev DB. **(4) Standards reinforced**: `.form-error-banner` + `.field-error` CSS already shipped in VALID-1; `json_validation_error(array $fields, string $message)` in `api/bootstrap.php` is now the ONLY way form APIs should report validation errors (422, `error.code='VALIDATION_ERROR'`, `error.fields` map). `json_error('MISSING_REQUIRED', …)` fail-fast pattern is retired for form endpoints. Every client submit handler follows the shape: `if (!this.validateX()) return; this.busy = true; try { const r = await FF_Api.post(...); if (r.success) { FF_Toast.success(...); this.xOpen = false; await this.load(); } else { this._paintErrors(this.xErrors, 'xFormError', r, '…'); } } catch(e) { this.xFormError = 'Network error. Please try again.'; } this.busy = false;`. **Stop conditions all ✅**: every form has field-level errors that appear inline (not just a top banner), every validation message is spec-exact, every server field key maps back to its UI slot, duplicate/lookup errors route to the offending field, the smoke test proves the envelope shape is identical across all 30 endpoints. |

## Model B Mileage Refactor — Multi-Session Master Plan

### Overview — Avi's intended Model B billing model
Optional per-lease precharge toggle. When `precharge_enabled=1`:
- Lease stores `precharge_amount` (operator-set, NOT derived from `estimated_mileage`) and running `precharge_balance`.
- Invoice 1 emits a visible "Mileage Precharge" line for the full `precharge_amount` — customer pays upfront.
- Each subsequent invoice (monthly cron OR ad-hoc manual) shows TWO visible mileage lines: usage at per-km/mile rate, and a precharge credit drawing the balance down. Net mileage = usage − credit.
- Balance decrements by the credit applied each period. When balance hits zero, future invoices bill straight per-km with no credit line.
- At lease close: positive remaining balance refunded via toggle — cash refund (DR AR / CR Cash) or account credit (credit_note row, `source='mileage_overpayment'`). One-time customers' unused credits must be convertible to cash later.

Customers without precharge (`precharge_enabled=0`): straight per-km billing each invoice, no allowance, no review gate, no drawdown logic. Model B Lite (D135 configuration).

### Dispatch contract reference
S-INVOICE-DISPLAY-COMPREHENSIVE (commits 8bc4e5c + aabb087 + 5dc2af2 + df1bd20 + f9130a2 + ea98362 — see SESSION LOG entry on 2026-05-11; brought to main via merge commit ab122eb on 2026-05-12) placed forward-looking markers **exclusively in app/admin/invoices/show.php** (InvoiceGenerator.php was NOT touched in that arc):

- **LINE TYPE DISPATCH CONTRACT comment block** at app/admin/invoices/show.php:1866-1906 (comment 1866-1886 + `$itemTypeBadge` match table 1889-1906).
  - Current supported item_type values (from show.php:1879-1881 + DB ENUM at FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql:1898): `base_rental`, `mileage_precharge`, `mileage_adjustment`, `mileage_credit`, `insurance`, `warranty`, `late_fee`, `early_return_credit`, `manual_adjustment`, `damage`, `discount`, `account_credit_applied`, `other`, `gps` (14 values).
  - Pending types per show.php:1882-1885 (S-MILEAGE-2B scope): `mileage_drawdown_credit`, `mileage_usage`.
  - Note: `mileage_precharge` is supported in display but NOT EMITTED by any production code today (per S-MILEAGE-MODEL-AUDIT 2026-05-04). S-MILEAGE-2A is the first production emit path.
- **Dual S-MILEAGE-2A/2B extension point markers** in show.php:
  - PHP-side at lines 1769-1782 (taxable subtotal docblock with explicit "S-MILEAGE-2A/2B note" at 1775-1781)
  - HTML-side at line 2182 (template comment: "Model B mileage breakdown (usage − credit) slots here between line items aggregate and tax block")
- **lib/Billing/InvoiceGenerator.php** carries NO S-MILEAGE-2A/2B markers today. S-MILEAGE-2A will place engine-side markers at the precharge emit site as part of that work.

Each session in the refactor arc extends these dispatch contracts before adding business logic. New line type → confirm ENUM value exists (or add migration) → confirm match case exists (or add case) → confirm display template handles the shape → wire engine emit → add tests.

### Hybrid state contract
Between 2A ship and 2B ship, FleetForge is in hybrid Model B/C state:
- `precharge_enabled=1` leases: Invoice 1 is Model B (precharge line). Invoice 2+ is Model C (per-period excess gate). Live-coherent by design.
- `precharge_enabled=0` leases: All invoices use Model B Lite (straight per-km, no excess gate if `estimated_mileage=0`) per D135.
- Model C scaffolding (S-LEASE-MILEAGE manager review gate, priorExcessKm safeguard): NOT deleted until S-MILEAGE-3. The priorExcessKm safeguard in particular must survive until S-MILEAGE-3 explicitly retires it.

### Out-of-scope-but-tracked items
- Bug 1: "Cumulative Total" label on invoice show page is misleading (should read "Lease-to-Date Distance"). Rider on S-MILEAGE-2B.
- Bug 4: soft validation when `billing_period_start < lease.start_date`. Rider on S-MILEAGE-2B.
- Close-time refund toggle (cash vs credit): S-MILEAGE-3.
- Customer portal rendering of precharge balance: S-MILEAGE-4 placeholder.
- priorExcessKm safeguard deletion: S-MILEAGE-3 (NOT 2B).

### Test strategy
- Per-session integration tests: each session in the arc includes its own T8/T10/T12 integration tests.
- Scenario test suite: S-MILEAGE-5 ships 20 hermetic scenarios using SamsaraClient fixture mode (FIX_STD, FIX_PARKED, FIX_NONE, FIX_RESET, FIX_SPARSE, FIX_GAP per lib/Samsara/FixtureProvider.php).
- D132 extension: S-MILEAGE-2A must extend the rate-tier completeness invariant to cover `precharge_amount` when `precharge_enabled=1` (smoke invariant I7). DB-side `chk_leases_precharge_amount` CHECK at FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql:2248 already enforces; I7 makes the gate doc-asserted by the smoke suite, not only DB-asserted by the CHECK.
- Fixture mode flag: settings key `samsara.fixture_mode` (lib/GPS/SamsaraClient.php:1259 dispatch path) — set to `'1'` (string) in all test contexts; reset on exit. Never test against live Samsara.

DB_SANITIZE_COLUMN (S016):
  db_sanitize_column() backtick-quotes every column name.
  Reason: `condition` is a MySQL reserved word.

FF_API.POST:
  - ALWAYS use base_url() — never bare relative strings.
  - ALWAYS resolves: check d.error in .then(), never use .catch() for business errors.
  - Sends JSON. For file uploads use raw fetch() + FormData + both CSRF headers.

CSRF TRAP: Raw fetch() MUST include both headers:
  'X-Requested-With': 'XMLHttpRequest'
  'X-CSRF-Token': document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]')?.content ?? ''

PORTAL AUTH: Portal uses separate session key ff_portal_user (not ff_user).
  portal_customer_id() for data isolation. portal_is_primary() for sub-user mgmt.
  Portal CSS classes: portal-* prefix.

CSS: .form-control (NOT .form-input) | .table | .stat-grid | .detail-grid
     base_url('api/v1/...') — api_url() does NOT exist
     Badges: badge-success/warning/danger/info/neutral

S-PROD-1B KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
  • D14 invoice immutability is unconditional — no role exemption. The is_super_admin()
    check in the guard was a latent CRA compliance hole. Any future financial-field guard
    must apply to ALL callers without exception.
  • Full-PUT roundtrip pattern: when blocking a field post-send, compare submitted value
    against DB value rather than blocking on presence alone. Blocking notes by presence
    broke every form that re-posted the full invoice body unchanged.
  • Optimistic lock comparisons: NEVER use raw string equality on updated_at timestamps.
    Always normalise via DateTimeImmutable::getTimestamp() (Unix seconds). DST and driver
    microsecond padding both cause spurious 409s with raw string comparison.
  • MFA auto-set belongs at the role-mutation callsite, not in a migration. Any time
    users.role_id changes, recompute mfa_required from the new role's slug against
    security.mfa.required_roles. Demote lifts requirement only — never clear mfa_enabled
    or mfa_secret (D-E).
  • Reconcile scripts follow the S-FIX-2 pattern: default dry-run, --execute requires
    interactive 'yes', single db_transaction, per-row audit_log. Always audit dry-run
    output with the user before running --execute.

S-PROD-2 KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
  • Sentry must be wired in bootstrap.php before session start so early crashes (DB
    connect fail, config parse error) are captured. Wiring it after auth means pre-auth
    errors are invisible in Sentry.
  • PII scrub in before_send needs TWO layers: key-name matching (password, api_key, etc.)
    AND value-pattern matching (bcrypt $2y$ prefix, ENC: AES ciphertext). Key-name alone
    misses secrets stored under unexpected keys; value-pattern alone is too broad.
  • SNS webhook contract: ALWAYS return HTTP 200 on valid signatures. Only 403 on sig
    failure. NEVER 5xx — SNS interprets that as a transient error and retries indefinitely,
    causing duplicate DB writes and audit log noise.
  • stream.php SSE compatibility: bootstrap.php sets Content-Type: application/json
    early, but stream.php overrides with Content-Type: text/event-stream before any output.
    The override is safe because PHP header() replaces rather than appends. Pre-SSE errors
    correctly use json_error(); post-SSE sendSSE() calls are a different format and must
    not be touched.
  • AI files had loaded config/app.php + auth.php directly, bypassing CSRF enforcement,
    Sentry capture, and json_error(). The correct pattern for all API files is
    bootstrap.php, which provides all of these. Direct config/auth loading is a red flag.
  • json_error() is a never-returning function — it calls exit() internally. Never add
    an explicit exit after it; doing so is dead code and misleads readers about control flow.

S-MILEAGE-1 KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
  • Backup table leases_precharge_backup_S_MILEAGE_1 captured 34 rows from the dropped
    Model A columns. All rows had mileage_precharge_amount=0.00 and
    mileage_precharge_invoiced=0. No real precharge data existed under Model A
    scaffolding — the audit's "zero writers" finding was substantively correct, but a
    default-value INSERT path was writing zeros on lease creation. Confirmed safe to
    proceed with Model B refactor. Backup table retained as audit trail; cleanup

S-CLEANUP-LBP-COLS-2 KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
